newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Opel output in Portugal okay until Monday.
newsitem.headline: Opel output in Portugal okay until Monday.

text.p: Production of Opel pickups and vans in Portugal is guaranteed to continue normally until at least Monday despite the French truckers' strike, a spokesman said.
"We have normal production guaranteed for tomorrow and Monday," Miguel Tome told Reuters.
The factory at Azambuja, 30 miles (48 km) north of Lisbon, normally shuts over the weekend.
Tome said Opel would decide on Monday whether to reduce or halt production from Tuesday, depending on events in France and the company's ability to get supplies.

Opel had taken special steps to bring in bodywork, engines, gearboxes and air bags via air, boat and train to Barcelona and then into Portugal by road, Tome said. Before the strike, the parts were delivered just by road.
The Azumbuja factory, which produces Opel Combo pickups and Opel Corsa vans, was so far producing its normal output of 240 vehicles per day, Tome said.

Earlier, Portugal's biggest car manufacturer, the Ford-Volkswagen AutoEuropa joint venture, said it would halt production on Friday because the French strike had made it difficult to receive supplies.
Striking truck drivers voted to keep up their 11-day stranglehold on the French economy on Thursday, defying government calls to return to work after talks with bosses collapsed over pay demands.
